pages.c26-p01: Define an operating system, describe its main functions and give examples for different devices
pages.c26-p02: Explain how an operating system manages processes, multitasking and memory
pages.c26-p03: Describe how file systems organise data and use basic command-line instructions
pages.c26-p04: Explain how operating system updates, user accounts, permissions and built-in security features protect a computer
pages.c26-p05: Compare open-source and proprietary software and describe the role of Linux

q.q: What is an operating system?
o: Software that manages hardware and software

q.q: What type of software is an operating system?
Where does the OS sit?
o: Between the hardware and the apps

q.q: What does booting mean?
o: Starting a computer and loading the OS

q.q: What is a device driver?
o: Software that lets the OS control hardware

q.q: Which OS function shares the CPU between programs?
Which OS function organises data into files and folders?
Which OS function decides what's in RAM?
Which OS function controls who can log in?
Which is a desktop operating system?
Which is a phone operating system?
Which OS is used on many school Chromebooks?
Which kind of OS is used in airbags and pacemakers?
Which is NOT an operating system?
What is a process?
Why might each browser tab run as a separate process?
o: So one crashing tab doesn't crash the whole browser

q.q: Which tool shows running processes on Windows?
Which tool shows running processes on a Mac?
What is multitasking?
o: Running more than one program at a time

q.q: How does a single CPU core multitask?
o: It runs every program at the same instant
The OS switches between processes very quickly

q.q: What is scheduling?
o: Deciding which process uses the CPU and for how long

q.q: How can a multi-core CPU help multitasking?
o: Each core can run a different process at the same time

q.q: What is RAM used for?
o: Holding programs and data currently in use

q.q: What is virtual memory?
o: Storage used as extra memory when RAM is full

q.q: Why does relying on virtual memory slow a computer?
o: Storage is much slower than RAM

q.q: Why does the OS keep each process in its own memory area?
o: So programs can't read or damage each other's data

q.q: Which is a background process?
What is a quick way to free up RAM?
o: Close apps and tabs you aren't using

q.q: What is a file system?
o: The part of the OS that organises data on storage

q.q: What is a directory?
What is the top level of a file hierarchy called?
What is a file path?
o: The full location of a file
q.why: Every folder from the root down.

q.q: Which is a valid Windows file path?
q.why: Windows uses drive letters and backslashes.

q.q: Which separator do Mac and Linux paths use?
What does a file extension show?

Which extension runs a program on Windows?
Why is "photo.jpg.exe" suspicious?
o: It's a program pretending to be an image

q.q: What is a command-line interface?
o: Controlling a computer by typing commands

q.q: Which command lists files on Mac/Linux?
Which command changes folder?
Which command makes a new folder?
What does "cd .." do?
What does pwd show on Mac/Linux?
Why do IT technicians use the command line?
o: It's fast and tasks can be automated with scripts

q.q: Why is the command line used on many servers?
o: Servers often have no screen or graphical interface

q.q: What is a vulnerability?
o: A weakness that attackers could exploit

q.q: What is a patch?
o: An update that fixes a bug or vulnerability

q.q: Why is it risky to delay security updates?
o: Attackers target known holes on unpatched computers

q.q: What does end of support mean?
o: The maker stops releasing updates and security fixes

q.q: When did Windows 10 reach end of support?
What is the risk of using an unsupported OS?
What can an administrator account do that a standard account can't?
o: Install software and change system settings

q.q: Why use a standard account day to day?
o: Malware can't easily make system-wide changes

q.q: What are permissions?
o: Rules controlling what users and apps can do

q.q: Which permission request from a torch app is suspicious?
What is sandboxing?
o: Running apps in a restricted area

q.q: What does a firewall do?
What is Microsoft Defender?
What does drive encryption protect against?
o: Someone reading your data if the laptop is stolen

q.q: Which is a secure sign-in method?
o: Fingerprint or face recognition with a PIN
Password written on a sticky note

q.q: How can old laptops that can't run Windows 11 be reused?
o: Install a lightweight Linux OS or ChromeOS Flex
Keep using an unsupported OS forever

q.q: What is source code?
What is open-source software?
o: Software whose code is public and can be changed and shared

q.q: What is proprietary software?
o: Software owned by a company, with secret code

q.q: Which is open-source software?
Which is proprietary software?
What is a software licence?
o: A legal agreement about how software can be used

q.q: Who created Linux?

What is a Linux distro?
o: A version of Linux, such as Ubuntu

What is the kernel?
o: The core of an operating system

q.q: Which is an argument for open source?
o: Anyone can check the code for security problems
No one can see the code

q.q: Which is an argument against open source for some users?
o: Some popular software and games don't run on it

q.q: Which is an advantage of proprietary software?
Why might a charity choose Linux for old laptops?
o: It's free and runs well on older hardware

What is an NPU?
o: A chip designed to run AI tasks

q.q: What is on-device AI?
o: AI that runs on the device itself
AI that only runs in the cloud

q.q: Which is a benefit of on-device AI?
o: It can work offline and keep data private

q.q: Which is an AI feature in modern operating systems?
o: A command to delete the OS

q.q: What is an AI agent?
o: AI that carries out multi-step tasks for you

q.q: Why are permissions especially important for AI agents?
o: They could take actions like sending messages or buying things

q.q: Which is a privacy concern about AI in the OS?
o: The AI may see everything on your screen

q.q: Why did a planned AI screenshot-history feature cause concern?
o: It recorded users' screen activity, raising privacy risks
q.why: It was changed to be off by default and encrypted.

q.q: How could attackers misuse an AI agent?
o: Tricking it with hidden instructions into doing harmful things

q.q: What is a cloud-based OS?
o: An OS that runs most apps and stores most files online

q.q: Why do many schools use cloud-based OS devices?
o: They're cheap and easy to manage

q.q: Which OS is designed for a mixed reality headset?
What does "over-the-air update" mean for a car?
o: It's fixed in a garage only

q.q: Which is an accessibility benefit of AI in operating systems?
Which rule makes an AI agent safer?
o: Ask the user before sending, buying or deleting
